name: Hem trousers
blurb: A proper hem — measured, pressed, and stitched so it is invisible from the outside — saves a tailor’s fee every time you buy trousers, and takes an evening to learn.
gear: Needle and thread, or a machine
steps: Wear the trousers with the shoes you will wear them with, and have someone pin the fold at the right length. Do both legs — they are rarely identical.
Turn inside out, measure the pin line, and mark a consistent line all round with chalk.
Add the hem allowance below the line — usually 3 to 4 cm — and cut off the excess.
Press the raw edge under by 1 cm, then fold up to the marked line and press again. Pressing is what makes the hem crisp.
Stitch with a blind hem — catching only a thread or two of the outer fabric — by hand or with a machine blind-hem foot.
Press the finished hem and check both legs match on the body.
tips: Measure twice with the actual shoes. Different shoes change the break by centimetres.
Keep the original hem if the fabric has a distinctive edge: it can be detached and reattached.
proof: Both legs hang at the same, correct length and the stitching is invisible from outside.
